teacherPlayback: Two complete playbacks controlled by the teacher. No student media controls.
scoreRule: 6 objectively scored multiple-choice tasks and 2 teacher-reviewed written tasks, 1 point each. Proposed grade only after both written tasks reviewed.
notes: Authentic dialogue includes aggression and profanity. Teacher must check age suitability and source recording.

objective.q: What makes this serious conversation funny at times?
options: Everyone has prepared jokes
Unexpected interruptions break up strict warnings
The men are watching a comedy
All the rules are easy to follow
objective.explanation: The questions interrupt an angry and serious speech.
objective.sourceEvidence: Unexpected remarks create humour during warnings.

objective.q: Why is the complaint about uniforms important?
options: The uniforms are not clean
Everybody wants to wear one
The men are preparing for a parade
They remind the group of existing tensions
objective.explanation: Uniforms refer to a group that provokes conflict.
objective.sourceEvidence: A man complains that uniforms were not supposed to be there.

objective.q: How does the speaker respond when someone says he broke a promise?
options: He briefly acknowledges it and moves on
He changes all the rules
He asks everyone to vote
He apologises and leaves
objective.explanation: He uses a brief concession, then continues.
objective.sourceEvidence: He says 'Nevertheless' after the uniform objection.

objective.q: What happens when somebody asks about 'snow'?
options: The men go outside
The wedding is delayed
The question interrupts and leads to more rules
The speaker agrees to stop talking
objective.explanation: The unexpected question disrupts the serious instructions.
objective.sourceEvidence: The snow exchange produces further refusals.

objective.q: Why does the speaker mention Grace?
options: She has written the list of rules
He wants the men to behave for her sake
She is waiting to explain her plans
He wants her to leave the event
objective.explanation: He uses concern for Grace to support the instructions.
objective.sourceEvidence: He does not want Grace embarrassed.

objective.q: Why does he repeat the last warning?
options: The others cannot speak English
He has forgotten the earlier orders
The wedding has already started
He is worried his instructions will not be followed
objective.explanation: The repetition shows urgency and an effort to enforce authority.
objective.sourceEvidence: The final order grows more forceful.

written.q: Describe one interruption and explain how it changes the conversation.
written.modelAnswer: The question about snow interrupts the serious warning and leads to more restrictions.
written.teacherCriterion: Identify one real interruption and a sensible effect.
written.sourceEvidence: Interjections interrupt his attempt to control the discussion.

written.q: What behaviour does the main speaker want from the men for Grace's sake?
written.modelAnswer: He wants them not to fight or cause trouble at the wedding.
written.teacherCriterion: One supported connection between avoiding trouble and Grace.
written.sourceEvidence: He says not to embarrass Grace.
